How should I approach this matchup?

Crow Charmer is possibly one of the more equal match-ups against Puppet Master. Murmurate can simultaneously deal with puppet moves like Puppet Barrage, as well as hitting Mechamaru. It also gives Mei Mei burst if Mechamaru still gets to hit, as the puppets are counted as seperate NPCs. Her teleport can also be used in some niche scenarios to avoid getting hit, such as retreating from Puppet Barrage or going above moves like Ultra Spin or Heat Emission. Despite this, Mechamaru still has a slight advantage over Mei Mei due to having a true damage combo, Offload just being stupidly strong, and stronger neutral and range. Manage your neutral and cooldowns well. This is especially important for Mei Mei as she can punish pretty hard if you play recklessly. If Mei Mei hits a puppet with Murmurate, do not rush in and punish, as it ends up giving her burst and you're the one getting punished Other than that, it's all mostly observe and adapt. Mei Mei can change how she plays whenever she wants due to how good her kit is designed, so I can't just tell you to play a certain way and it will work.
How should I approach this matchup?

DETACH + AERIAL 4 IF THEY PLAY NORMALLY The best I can think of is using a puppet to block Detach. Play as usual, Kuro usually won't be able to win. Offloaded Ultra Cannon can be used to also block a Hanami's front dash, as well as letting the Mechamaru go above Flower Field by using the puppet's head to go above the hitbox.

A majority of neutral counterplay against Puppet Master is to save your dashes to retreat from any unfavorable scenario the player finds themselves in. There are a total of three to four moves that a Puppet Master has that they can use in neutral, depending on their playstyle. Do note that a skilled [noauto]Puppet Master[/noauto] will use a combination of their neutral tools to overwhelm your defenses, so the key points in shutting down his neutral is to [color=hsl(217, 91%, 60%)]keep calm, read, and adapt to the situation accordingly.[/color] [u][i]Puppet Barrage[/i] (RR)[/u] is a pressure tool used to force the player to either block, retreat, or use a move with lingering i-frames. Retreating by moving away from the Puppet Master and then blocking once the puppets dash if they're at range. This saves a dash that can be used to retreat against other moves, or to gain an advantage if the [noauto]Puppet Master[/noauto] goes for an M1 trade. Alternatively, certain characters can use their mobility or AoE moves here to also deal with the puppets, though this is extremely niche and might lead to the opposing player getting punished if the move puts them in a noticeable amount of stun time. [u][i]Offloaded Ultra Spin[/i] (R1)[/u] is a neutral tool most often used at the midrange when the puppet can spawn behind the opponent, forcing the opposing player to block the puppet and leave their back exposed. At close range, the opposing player can side dash out of the R1's path safely. Alternatively, if both players are at mid range, then your options start to differ: if they leave Heat Emission's effective range, then side dash away. If not, block the R1 and react to whatever follow-up they go for afterwards. [u][i]Heat Emission[/i] (4)[/u] is the strongest move Puppet Master has in neutral. It's a midrange rush move with a big AoE explosion at the front that CANNOT be blocked or countered on base, and is usually the straw the breaks the camel's back if side dash is on cooldown. Stay out of it's effective range as much as possible. If you are within range and the Puppet Master uses it, use your side dash to retreat.

You have to factor in two things when encountering an opponent The preferred playstyle of their character The choices they make to enforce their preferred playstyle The most important factor is the preferred playstyle of their character. You will punish the wrong choices they make to enforce it (i.e. a bad front dash) and prevent the “correct” choices from punishing you. Most playstyles can be broken under two categories: Rushdown and Zoner. The definitions should not be taken too literally, but most characters operate better depending on their range from their opponent. Reggie is the cog in this, as he can be either Rushdown or Zoner. Here is how you should play against these playstyles:

Characters who you should look out for are: Yuji, Naoya, and Todo Since your opponent will always want to approach you, you must counter that. Your most important moves are Gushing Wound, Garage Sale, and Littering. You must use these to keep range. Gushing Wound should always be thrown out in further engagements (when there is more of a distance between you and the opponent) to slow down their approach. Garage Sale does a similar job to Gushing Wound in keeping them out, but can be used in closer engagements to push them away. Littering should be used in a fashion similar to Choso’s Blood Orb that is left behind by Aerial Flowing Red Scale, giving yourself an area where you are immune from combos (you can activate Littering while stunned).

Characters you should look out for are: Ryu, Hanami, and Haruta. Since your opponent wants to stay as far away from you as possible, you must use your pokes and range closing tools to counter that. The most important ones are Gushing Wound, Garage Sale, and Red Seal Speed Crash. These options will slow down their means of running, Gushing Wound stuns them for a bit when hit (they won’t typically be blocking since they’re running), Garage Sale stuns them, and Speed Crash (especially Red Seal) is great at closing the gap fast. These are all suggestions, and oftentimes in gameplay, you do not need to follow these ideas, but they are generally the standard answers for these playstyles.

Although Register does not have any specified combos, these should be kept in mind: [kbd]Blunt Trauma[/kbd] -> [kbd]Speed Crash[/kbd] [kbd]SpeedCrash[/kbd] -> [kbd]Blunt Trauma[/kbd] [kbd]Piano Drop[/kbd] -> [kbd]Garage Sale[/kbd] / [kbd]Blunt Trauma[/kbd] / [kbd]Littering[/kbd] [kbd]Littering [/kbd]-> [kbd]Garage Sale[/kbd] / [kbd]Piano Drop[/kbd] / [kbd]Speed Crash[/kbd] / [kbd]Blunt Trauma[/kbd]

These moves should only be used during passive moments, especially the start of the match. These moves are not necessary for Register to function, though the buffs provided may offer possible mixups. In any other situation, it is better to discard off these moves when given. Keep in mind that it is not meant to discourage the use of [color=hsl(3, 93%, 63%)]Red Seal[/color] moves, but it is oftentimes more optimal to discard Coupon for another move instead of trading it for a 8 second cooldown and a slightly buffed move. Discarding Coupon also has its own perks, since it allows you to immediately have a move off cooldown (assuming you did not use any prior move).

The combination of Coupon and Extra Coupon ([i]Super Coupon[/i]) may introduce interesting dynamics, but is generally not advisable to do in the midst of combat. If the opponent is lousy, however, it may be fine to use. Gushing Wound is part of Register's initial starting kit. This allows for the quick use of a poke, and if landed, chips down the opponent by 12. The move is unblockable, and if not blocked, it serves as a great interruption tool for further range opponents. The move itself has a range of ~200 studs, and has the perk of being fast, which is great for stopping Ryu from clearing his resource easily or halting runners. This move can catch many off guard with its small windup, fast speed, and range, and is generally very safe to use freely.

Blunt Trauma is a powerful move in Register's kit. It serves as a punishing option after ragdoll, but one should keep in mind that whiffing the move is very punishable. The effect provided by the move makes it easy to follow up and harder to punish, since once hit, they cannot side dash and are susceptible to further attack. One must absolutely not use this outside of extending in combos, since the blockable natural of it makes it easy to counter. The usual reaction to this is to front dash away, so using Garage Sale as a follow-up is nice. Red Seal Blunt Trauma is very hard hitting, and it extends the debuff effect, however, it is the most evasive punishable move in Register's kit, since it leaves him out in the animation.

Restless Gambler is a scrappy brawler with tools intended to be able to used in almost any situation, which is meant to make him very well-rounded. However, as a result of little to no movement options and a lack of ranged options (outside of Reserve Balls), he ends up being a brawler who rarely gets an opening, making it so that every opportunity he gets must be capitalized on heavily. Restless Gambler gameplay mainly focuses around his second ability, Shutter Doors, as it provides combo extension, move variants, aerial mobility and can create a threat through the use of aerial Rough Energy. His neutral and disadvantage states are terrible due to his lack of good get-off-me tools and pokes, leading him to mainly rely on M1 trades to get much of anything done.

Try extending his combo's as much as possible, as this is a core part of restless gamblers kit. he also should use his low-cooldown projectile and knockback moves to catch opponents off-guard right as they try to counter-attack. ...Restless gambler also should: Frame-trap their block Abuse wall bounces Keep your mobility tool free

Restless Gambler likes to jump on doors. In all seriousness, his kit is compromised of simple techs that can spice up gameplay. This page is a WIP, so please, be patient for more. If you ever want to contribute to the wiki, please join the discord or just simply suggest your edits directly from this website!

Honored One generally M1 trades better and can invalidate your counter with Reversal Red and intentionally missing his moves. You can counter Rapid Punches after 1R but it can just as easily be baited out for more damage. Honored One Limitless can also catch you out of the air after jumping on shutter doors or during aerial 3, making these options significantly less viable in this matchup.

Use your counter to invalidate any wake-up shenanigans a Honored One player may try with 3. 1+2 can punish Lapse Blue on block and should be one of your main tools in this matchup. Keep the fight grounded, Honored One won't mind you going into the air to use Limitless on you to then lead into a 50/50 with 3.
What should you do versus them?

Restless Gambler generally outclasses Vessel in close combat altercations. Restless Gambler counter is a decent tool in this matchup as Vessel moves are very telegraphed, though he can feint. Although Vessel also has a lower HP pool than Restless Gambler, with some simple combos doing a majority of his HP. Fever Crush, as an example, would do 1/4th of a Vessel's health bar.

Be wary of Vessel's feints. A simple feint can put you into a bad spot, especially after a counter. Manji Kick can counter your Reserve Balls. Avoid trying to combo start with 1+2 as much in this matchup. You can attempt to bait out a Manji Kick by using Reserve Ball and then turning to a slightly different direction.
What should you do versus them?
A ditto is a ditto. Not much else to say here. The most notable thing in this matchup is that you can use aerial 3 to counter their aerial 3.

Salaryman, based off of the character Kento Nanami, is an intricate and technical character, specializing in burst damage and interrupting the opponent's attacks with timing. Performed accurately enough, Salaryman can inflict temporary debuffs to the enemy that make defending against your onslaught increasingly difficult. Neutral tools such as Cleaving Whirlwind and Blunt Cut keep your opponent on edge while you prepare your Ratio Point in order to break through their defenses. Salaryman offers unique combo routing that allows for powerful offense, regardless of if the opponent is stunned or not.

Salaryman works best either close or medium range from the enemy. Ensuring that a Ratio Point is always applied and that you get the maximum value out of the Ratio Point possible (Ratio Point variants, interruption staggers, etc.) will allow you to overwhelm and destroy your enemies in only a few interactions.

Salaryman's skills can be split into two sections: Close-range optimal and medium-range optimal. If you seek to use these moves in neutral, maintaining distance and timing will net you the best value. Also, you are in a much superior position when the enemy has a staggered limb, so aim to achieve that as soon as possible. Cleaving Whirlwind causes Salaryman to lunge a notable distance, so it can be used as a gap-closer from afar, followed up by a mix-up if you spin around the enemy to hit them behind their block. You can also punish enemies that use their own attacks too haphazardly by hitting them with the Ratio Point variant, interrupting and staggering their limb. Severance Kick gets most of its value in M1 trading. When you are blocking an enemy's onslaught of punches, weaving in Reverse Kick will stun the enemy long enough for you to punish them. Also, if most of your moves are all on cooldown but you have the enemy in an M1 chain, you can kick them away to gain enough distance to recover. Blunt Cut is punishable on block without Ratio Point, so avoid using it at all in neutral without it. If you hit an enemy with a Ratio Point, try to dash into them fast enough to convert off of it into more damage. Cross Cut is a consistent way, if you're fast enough, to get through a blocking opponent using the second half of the attack, which is unblockable no matter what. Finally, Stabilize, when used at the perfect distance, can stun opponents using attacks poorly without needing to use your Ratio Point. You can also try to use Stabilize in an M1 trade as you would with Reverse Kick to get the enemy off of you and give you a moment to prepare a Ratio Point.

This is expanded upon greatly in the Combos page, but there are still some details to know before bringing Salaryman into ranked matches: Severance Kick can be cancelled into Blunt Cut if the enemy does not block the kick. This is especially powerful with a Ratio Point applied Stabilize can be cancelled into both Cleaving Whirlwind and Blunt Cut with or without a Ratio Point so that you can keep up the pressure Making combos slower and more methodical can make it more likely for your enemy to try blocking or counter-attacking, which is when you should strike back with a Ratio Point variant, resetting the cooldown and giving you far more damage

Enemies very often use their evasive after being hit with Severance Kick, so try to condition them to use it by starting interactions with it. If they choose not to use it, you can instead cancel into Blunt Cut as mentioned before. There is a surprising amount of time you have to cancel into Blunt Cut, so once you're sure that they won't use their evasive, take initiative. Also, ragdolling your opponent in any way and then applying a Ratio Point (since they can see when you activate it) will pressure them to move before you convert into big damage with a well-timed Stabilize or Cleaving Whirlwind.

Salaryman other gimmick is interruptions, Some tied to Ratio Point while others are independent Not a rule of thumb but usually how it goes is: Interrupting without ratio (IWOR) makes the enemy receive more stun while those interruptions don't work on block, but they do against chase (Frontdash), m1s and skills Interrupting with ratio (IWR) debuffs the enemy while it also interrupts M1s, block, skills, dashes. Similar to Vessel's Divergent Fist

Nanami's greatest weakness are enemy's counter skills, making him even harder to play.
