The ratio Technique is tied to the R special button, also known as [b] Ratio Point [/b]. When pressed it starts a quick time event going over the target's head, visible to the Salaryman only. However the opposing player can figure out if it was activated by a distinct eye flash vfx, but he won't be aware if Salaryman succeeded in the QTE. The Ratio Point QTE is a bar positioned above the target's head. A circle slides on the bar and R has to be pressed again when the circle overlaps the red 7:3 line, if performed successfully, the opponent will be marked for the next 4.5 seconds, the timer will be displayed in the R special bar, going from empty to full for those 4.5 seconds. Ratio can be used in any stun, endlag, ragdoll The circle slides faster the lower the hp of the target is. Ratio Point also makes the attacks it affects deal more damage. Ratio Point allows Cleaving Whirlwind and Blunt Cut to get interruption properties. [b] POST UPDATE 1.78 [/b]: Ratio Point gets its Cooldown refreshed on interruption/hitting block with 1, 3, 4 skills Stabilise when imbued with ratio is now considered a strong block hitter due to its sheer speed

When ratio is successfully landed, some of Salaryman skills gain extra attributes. Which are: Cleaving Whirlwind bypasses block Severance Kick and reverse kick aren't affected Blunt Cut bypasses block Cross Cut (aerial blunt cut) hits block if Ratio Point is done on the first hit and it launches upwards if it's done on the second hit, the second hit bypasses block regardless. Stabilise hits block and stuns for longer (Stagger will be mentioned at interruptions) Uppercut does +4 damage and it ragdols further, extending to Cleaving Whirlwind (consistent) or fully charged Blunt Cut (inconsistent) 4th M1 does +4 damage and it ragdols further.

By using Salaryman's fourth M1 on someone who has a Ratio Point on them, the M1 will deal double the damage, totaling to 8 (10 in Overtime), as well as knocking the enemy substantially farther back. In Overtime, this M1 becomes unblockable.

By using Salaryman's uppercut on someone who has a Ratio Point on them, the upperut will deal double the damage, totaling to 8 (10 in Overtime), as well as knocking the enemy substantially farther up in the air, allowing you to hit the enemy with Cleaving Whirlwind if aimed properly during their descent. In Overtime, this uppercut becomes unblockable.

When Salaryman is in Overtime, having a Ratio Point on the opponent allows your downslam to also have a Black Flash variant, like how your fourth M1 and uppercut normally do, dealing twice the damage as a regular downslam, totaling to 10.

A lunging strike that is blockable from the front, accompanied with melee i-frames to make it easier to get in someone's face. Salaryman arms his cleaver and spins forward, slashing downward and dealing 12 damage upon connection, pushing the enemy back and ragdolling them. It has a 16-second cooldown.

Cleaving Whirlwind is a consistent neutral pressure tool. You can attempt to spin your character behind the opponent's block if they anticipate it to knock them down. With 46 frames of startup, it is certainly reactable, but you can definitely play mind games.

Cleaving Whirlwind can be seamlessly cancelled into if Salaryman uses the attack right after successfully hitting Stabilize. If it is the Stabilize Ratio Point variant, you can guarantee a strike with Cleaving Whirlwind, since the enemy is unable to block.

As mentioned above, Salaryman has melee i-frames throughout the startup and active frames. This allows you to avoid people's attempts to cancel your strike with an M1, barrage attack (Like Locust Guy's Clever) or grab attack (Like Cursed Partners' Second Wind).

Like the normal version of Cleaving Whirlwind, Salaryman lunges forward, spinning and striking the opponent. With a ratio point applied to the target, the strike deals an additional 4 damage, totaling to 16 damage. If the attack either hits a blocking enemy or interrupts the enemy, their right arm will be staggered. This shrinks their blocking angle substantially for 7 seconds. It will also immediately reset your special's cooldown.

A quick forward kick delivered by Salaryman that pushes enemies forward a slight distance. The kick itself deals 12 damage. However, it has the unique property of being able to launch throwables at high speeds, similar to Vessel's special. This kicked throwable deals 15 damage. Lastly, if the enemy does not use their evasive, blunt cut can be seamlessly cancelled into after the kick connects. The kick does not remove the Ratio Point from the enemy.

By holding backwards and using Severance Kick, Salaryman will instead perform Reverse Kick. This deals exactly the same damage as the normal severance kick, with the added bonus of both being unblockable and stunning enemies upon interruption (similar to Vessel's Divergent Fist, but not on block). By utilizing this variant during an M1 trade, you can very easily interrupt the enemy's M1, stunning them and guaranteeing yourself plenty of damage. Do note that, unlike the default kick, Reverse Kick can not be cancelled into Blunt Cut.

A charged slice through the enemy. The charging will adjust Salaryman's distance traveled, as well as the damage dealt. Salaryman holds his arm behind his shoulder, holding a stance for a moment before releasing his momentum and firing past the enemy in front of him, cutting anyone in his path, dealing 9 (14 if you interrupt someone) damage. It has a 16-second cooldown. Using Blunt Cut within a short period of time after successfully hitting Severance Kick will allow you to seamlessly cancel into it, disregarding the charging animation.

As a general rule-of-thumb, Blunt Cut should never, ever, ever be used in neutral without a Ratio Point applied or if the enemy is ragdolled. It has a very obvious wind-up and you will be left right in front of the enemy in blocked.

Ratio-less Blunt Cut will usually be resorted to being used at a medium-distance if the enemy is ragdolled and knocked away by another move, likely Cleaving Whirlwind. Since it can be cancelled into through Severance Kick, it is very often to use it following that move as well, giving you a chance to continue the offensive.

After using Severance Kick, you have a surprisingly long duration to cancel into Blunt Cut, so much so that you can actually begin moving again and still instantly use the move. This forgiving period lets you apply a Ratio Point to maximize damage and debuff affliction.

When Ratio Point is applied to a target, using Blunt Cut through them will make the attack unblockable, as well as dealing an additional 4 damage, up to a maximum of 18 damage if fully charged. If the attack either hits a blocking enemy or interrupts the enemy, their left leg will be staggered. This makes the enemy completely unable to dash for 7 seconds. It will also immediately reset your special's cooldown.

If airborne when using Blunt Cut, Salaryman will instead glide down, slamming the ground and anyone directly beneath him. This first slam is blockable, otherwise dealing 5 damage. If the initial slam hits an enemy, regardless of if they are blocking or not, a second strike will automatically be used, this time being unblockable, dealing 4 damage, and sending the enemy tumbling back (though they will remain standing). As a side note, if the first slam is hit on a ragdolled opponent, they will be unable to use their ragdoll cancel so that the second hit can connect.

The Ratio Point variant of Cross Cut innately has two sub-variants depending on when the Ratio Point is applied onto the enemy. If the first slam connects whilst the enemy has a Ratio Point applied, the slam will deal an additional 6 damage and making the slam unblockable. If the slam interrupts or hits an opponent's block, it will stagger their left leg (see Blunt Cut: Ratio Point), as well as resetting your special's cooldown. If the Ratio Point is not applied until right before the second slash of the attack hits, it will instead amplify the latter half of the attack, increasing the slice's damage by 6, throwing the enemy upwards and ragdolled. If the slice interrupts or hits an opponent's block, it will stagger their right arm (see Cleaving Whirlwind: Ratio Point), as well as resetting your special's cooldown. The angle of the second Ratio Point variant allows Cleaving Whirlwind to be smoothly hit while the enemy is falling back down, if aimed correctly. Theoretically, though very difficult and situational, both ratio strikes can be hit in a single Cross Cut if the enemy is interrupted with the first ratio slam (resetting your special cooldown), and you re-apply a ratio on the enemy before the second slice connects. This will deal a total of 21 damage.

Salaryman reels their arm back and thrusts their cleaver forward, crushing the opponent's stomach, dealing 6 damage and pushing the enemy back. If Stabilize interrupts an opponent's attack, it will do a prolonged stagger where the enemy clutches their stomach longer, and Salaryman twirls his cleaver. This is a great time to apply a Ratio Point, as the enemy will be stunned long enough for it to be done safely. Additionally, after Stabilize connects, the endlag can be cut short by using either Cleaving Whirlwind or Blunt Cut immediately after.

If the enemy is hit with Stabilize while a ratio is applied to them, the aforementioned interruption stagger will trigger regardless of if the enemy was interrupted or not, dealing the same 6 damage. If the opponent is interrupted, it will deal a total of 10 damage, as well as resetting your special cooldown. It should be noted that, while Stabilize can hit ragdolled opponents, the ratio variant will not be used and the ratio itself will not be removed from the target.

Using your special places a 7:3 ratio on your opponents head for a moment. Pressing special again when the circle is on top of the red line locks it in place for 5 seconds. If you miss this timing, your special will be put on cooldown. This Ratio Point is the cornerstone of Salaryman's entire kit, granting him access to different properties to his M1s, as well as new variants for many of his moves. Hitting a Ratio Point variant with certain moves under certain conditions will stagger either the opponent's right arm or left leg. A staggered right arm drastically shortens the opponent's blocking angle for 7 seconds, and a staggered left leg makes the opponent unable to dash for 7 seconds. Interrupting an opponent with a Ratio Point variant will reset your special cooldown. In Overtime, there is no cooldown for your special. Base kit skills enhanced with Ratio Point: Fourth M1 Uppercut Cleaving Whirlwind Blunt Cut Cross Cut Stabilize Awakening skills enhanced with Ratio Point: Downslam Ratio Breaker I Ratio Breaker II Ratio Breaker III Ratio Breaker IV Sharpen Erosion Interrogate I Interrogate II Collapse I

One of the few ways to get a downslam with Salaryman in a combo, gives you ample time to set up Ratio. M1 (x3) Uppercut Severance Kick (Timed) M1 (x3) Downslam An incredibly consistent extender possible because hitting an airborne opponent with Severance Kick extends their ragdoll duration enough to get a downslam.

Flashier than the former, but you can't downslam after as easily. Priortize Ratio Point setup. M1 (x3) Uppercut (Head Surf) Severance Kick From here you can do a couple things after applying Ratio Point after the kick: Timed Cleaving Whirlwind on wakeup Cross Cut 2nd Half Ratio Point > Cleaving Whirlwind Timed Stabilize on wakeup > Charged Blunt Cut / Cleaving Whirlwind

Demanding timing but deals more damage at once. Severance Kick Side Dash Stabilize Blunt Cut The timing on this cancel is a little absurd and may not even be possible on your device. You'll need to time your side dash right when the animation for Severance Kick ends rather than spamming side dash. From here, hit the enemy with Stabilize and press Blunt Cut soon after.

Safely apply a Ratio Point before cancelling out of Severance Kick. Severance Kick Ratio Point Blunt Cut An often undermined part of Salaryman's kick is the window you have to cancel Severance Kick into Blunt Cut. Not only can you mix up the opponent before using it, but you can apply a Ratio Point after hitting the kick and you'd still have enough time to cancel.

Honored One's ability to both distance well and instantly get in your face makes it difficult for Salaryman to set up his Ratio Point. Also, Honored One's longer combos will cause your Ratio Point to run out and go on cooldown if you planted it ahead of time.

Generally, Salaryman has a rough time dealing with characters who have counters since it adds another variable into whether or not he will be able to interrupt an attack. However, Vessel's shorter combos as well as Salaryman's more burst-oriented playstyle gives him the slight advantage in most scenarios.

Same logic applies for counters here; Salaryman has to be consciously aware of Restless Gambler's special cooldown to avoid his interruptions getting... interrupted. Also, he is a victim of having Cleaving Whirlwind and Blunt Cut cancelled by Reserve Balls. At the same time, however, Salaryman can better close the gap and absolutely overwhelm him if he does not have a counter available, making this a pretty equal matchup.

Ten Shadows' absolute dominance in neutral 24/7 with Rabbit Escape and Divine Dogs: Totality being used in reaction to you charging attacks makes it very difficult for Salaryman to approach. Once you start getting combo'ed, you enter the same dilemma as with Honored One where is combos can be long enough to waste your Ratio Point, putting it on cooldown. Ten Shadows can retreat with his special in a pinch and can even react to Cleaving Whirlwind with Toad.

Perfection has a few tools that can very quickly let him get in Salaryman's face in reaction to charging moves, like blade mode front dash. Also, Soul Fire is a very easy way to shut down any of Salaryman's attempts to go on the offense.

It'll be a slaughter! Blood Manipulator's orbs will be a persistent obstacle for Salaryman, invalidating any and all approaches. Blood Manipulator also has a powerful counter to circumvent early interruption attempts, and he is capable of high-damaging combos like Salaryman . If Blood Manipulator chooses to play around his blood orb mines on the ground, he can launch himself away even if he is interrupted.

Switcher's recent buffs make him far more formidable in neutral, where Salaryman is meant to excel. When being swung at with Cleaving Whirlwind or Blunt Cut, Switcher can simply turn him away by clapping while looking in another direction. Additionally, he can feint his own skills with his clap to make Salaryman think he can successfully pull off an interrupt, thus allowing Switcher to punish him.

With Defense Attorney's ability to close in quickly and bypass blocks with their variants, this matchup may look overwhelmingly difficult for Salaryman initially. However, Salaryman had advantages that allow them to turn the tables on Defense Attorney. Firstly, while not a huge factor in this matchup, most of Salaryman's skills have very little endlag on whiff, which include [b]Stabilize[/b] and [b]Cleaving Whirlwind[/b]. This means that Defense Attorney can't get in [b]Extended Swings[/b]' Variant if Salaryman decides to throw out a skill and having to rely on Salaryman blocking or M1'ing. Secondly, while Defense Attorney prides themselves in being a character that can close in quickly and utilise many of their neutral options up close, Salaryman has various options to deal with this. [b]Stabilize[/b] having the ability to interrupt and even bypassing block with [b]Ratio[/b] while having such a quick windup means that Defense Attorney could get caught off guard and lose momentum, while Salaryman can convert into a combo with [b]Cleaving Whirlwind[/b] or [b]Blunt Cut[/b], with [b]Ratio[/b] if Defense Attorney had blocked during [b]Ratio Stabilize[/b]. [b]Severance Kick[/b] and [b]Backwards Kick[/b] are more situational, but can act as a tool that can keep Defense Attorney away, with the latter being able to lead into a combo if Defense Attorney was interrupted. Lastly, [b]Limb Staggering[/b] is a geniune problem for Defense Attorney. [b]Arm Stagger[/b] means that Defense Attorney has to play perfectly in neutral, as Salaryman can capitalise on their reduced block radius. [b]Leg Staggering[/b] means that Defense Attorney would partially struggle in their dashing mobility, and make it easier for Salaryman to win neutral or land [b]Ratio[/b] attacks that can't easily be avoided, such as [b]Cleaving Whirlwind[/b] and [b]Stabilize[/b]. Long story short, Salaryman has the tools to make close range neutral difficult for Defense Attorney, with [b]Ratio[/b] attacks being not easily avoidable up close and [b]Limb Staggering[/b] making it difficult to engage. Salaryman has the advantage in the long run.

When up against Cursed Partners, Salaryman's neutral becomes much harder. Options such as [b]Ratio Stabilize[/b] or [b]Backwards Kick[/b] may still be reliable up close, but Cursed Partners has many ways to engage from any distance that finding an opening may be difficult. [b]Second Wind[/b], [b]Veilstep[/b] and [b]Rika Launch[/b] provide easy and safe ways to close the gap while having virtually no windup, being able to catch Salaryman off guard or during windup such as during [b]Blunt Cut[/b]. [b]Outburst[/b] being able to parry or attack on its own after its animation makes neutral options such as [b]Ratio Cleaving Whirlwind[/b] much more difficult to land. Cursed Partners also has the more reliable evasive bait, such as [b]Air Rika Slam[/b] and [b]Resolute Slash[/b], while Salaryman lacks anything that stands out. Speaking of [b]Rika[/b], she makes closing in much harder for Salaryman. [b]Rika Slam[/b] and [b]Rika Haymaker[/b] provide ways to cover Cursed Partners during endlag or during M1 trades, with the former being able to convert into a combo much easier while the latter deals more damage on block and forces Salaryman to disengage. Even [b]Limb Staggering[/b] is less reliable since moves such as [b]Second Wind[/b] and [b]Ground or Air Rika Launch[/b] can help Cursed Partners stall its timer or engage even with their staggered limbs. In this matchup, Salaryman has to keep an eye out for the many options Cursed Partners has. Failing to do so usually results in Cursed Partners being able to convert into a combo, while Salaryman has to find a way to close in and land a [b]Ratio[/b] boosted attack, which will definitely prove difficult.

Easily one of the worst matchup Salaryman has. Puppet Master's sheer amount of options can keep Salaryman on their back foot for the entire encounter, while having incredibly safe options to engage from any distance. Up close, while Salaryman may look to have the advantage, [b]Offload Ultra Spin[/b] and [b]Boost On[/b] are moves that are hard to defend against since the former requires you to block towards your back, leaving you open for Puppet Master to attack, and the latter's windup being relatively quick and hard to evasive punish out of. At a distance, [b]Heat Emission[/b] is going to be your worst nightmare due to its wide range and being unblockable, while also having the ability to use the move early and catch Salaryman off guard when trying to avoid the attack. Moves such as [b]Puppet Barrage[/b] and [b]Offload Ultra Spin[/b] make avoiding this attack even harder and would usually result in Puppet Master converting into a combo. The final nail in the coffin is that almost all of Puppet Master's moves combo well into each other and are hard to punish most of the time, leaving Salaryman to react on the fly just to avoid and punish attacks Puppet Master can dish out. The best way Salaryman can win this is by closing in with [b]Limb Staggers[/b] to win M1 trades or utilizing [b]Ratio[/b] attacks such [b]Cleaving Whirlwind[/b] and [b]Blunt Cut[/b] to get in close. Other than that however, Salaryman is going to have an extremely hard time trying to keep up with Puppet Master's sheer amount of abilities to look out for and effective range they can start combos from.

Many of Head of the Hei's attacks leave him advantageous, but don't leave you fully stunned. You can very easily hit a bunch of interruptions with Cleaving Whirlwind and Stabilize, and also throw out Reversal Kick after he stabs you in an attempt to stun him. Also, since Salaryman's attacks are pretty mobile, it'll be harder for Head of the Hei to catch him with Decisive Strikes, among other moves.

As you'll learn with the Disaster Plants matchup, fighting a zoner is comparable to falling face-first into a pit full of unsterilized needles. Both the non-charged and charged versions of Granite Blast can be used on reaction to Salaryman's attempt to close the distance between them. And one of True Cannon's two melee skills make him fly into your face, not being very easy to interrupt.

This has got to genuinely be the worst matchup in the entire game. I'm not even joking! Disaster Plants' ever-present neutral domination, flower field to defend herself when being rushed with a move (Which Nanami is meant to excel at), R2 to safely approach when you're on defense, plethora of unblockable moves and latent fight potential by setting up spikes makes the Salaryman player want to actually slam their face into their desk.

Neutral presence is entirely equal between the two, despite having pretty different moves. Whoever gets the first M1 connection will be able to devastate the others' health bar. They also both have strong evasive bait and overall it is almost as equal as a mirror match itself.

Star Rage has THREE skills that can be utilized greatly at both close range to combat in Salaryman's range, as well as far range to completely destroy any hope for him. It will be very difficult for Salaryman to find a moment to strike when Star Rage is flailing about with unblockable, long range nuclear bombs every few moments.

Salaryman relies on side dashes to properly distance himself before using a skill in neutral to ensure it connects, as well as approaching after hitting an enemy with Severance Kick. With Aspiring Mangaka's ability to remove Salaryman's side dash entirely for a time, as well as being able to use a counter whenever he wants to protect himself from Salaryman's strong neutral tools make this matchup a little too tough.

Sky Bender is defined by her air focused kit, with her second m1 allowing her to slam down any opponent that's high in the sky. [multicolor=#9fffff,#9C88AA]Blind Rage[/multicolor] is a good combo starter, as she can snatch her opponents to bring them to the clouds if they're in m1 range. She also has a parry to projectiles, as [multicolor=#9fffff,#9C88AA]Sky Distortion[/multicolor] can be used as an attack whilst blowing back any projectile in her way. If Sky Bender's opponent is too far away from her, or if she knocked her opponent too far away, Sky Bender can close the gap between her and her enemies by using [multicolor=#ffffff,#9feeff]Sky Veil[/multicolor], in order to make her position invisible to her opponent, whilst gaining a speed boost when cloaked. This temporary invisibility allows her to approach without any concerns, as the enemy cannot see her during this timeframe. While invisible, she has access to her blockbreaking moves, so when close she's enough to her opponent, she can strike! This Innate technique makes little to no room for reaction time when it comes to her advances. Sky Bender's combos are not too difficult to pull off, although they do tend to give her opponents evasive fast. If she wants to make sure to avoid giving too much evasive, she can do combos high in the air to chain all of her moves, but this can cause some punishment on her end if she isn't careful with what she is doing. If the punish happens, it could lead to the match quickly being turned away from Sky Bender's favor. But if her cards are played right, she can dish out major damage that can easily decimate any opponent. Anyone who gets close to her gets demolished once she brings them to the clouds, making her a true sky bender.

Blind Rage's hitbox is pretty small, and with the newest update (as of typing this) getting rid of its ability to pick up ragdolled opponents, Blind Rage is best used in close range, or in a m1 chain. If Sky Bender wants to be stylish, and thinks she can time the grab after their uppercut (Blind Rage has the same properties of every other melee move, where it's possible to time the hitbox to land on ragdolled opponents while they're a certain height in the air), it is landable! She just needs to be mindful of the opponent's evasive meter. If Sky Bender's opponent evasives out of the grab, it will cause an automatic punishment on Sky Bender, resulting in her being true-ragdolled for 5 full seconds. This punish is blockable by Sky Bender, if she is not currently in her air m1, or if the air m1 was not missed via evasive.
Blind Rage (temper variant) has two powerful swings before the grab, both are blockable and the move to be punished on-reaction in the event of missing one of the two swings.

Sky Distortion is a pretty simple move. Sky Bender does a small twirl, grabbing the sky and hitting her opponents with it. If used in the air, it does a small lunge forward! If looking at your opponent while in the air and using it, it'll launch her horizontally towards her opponent, blocking or not. Do note that this does NOT hit ragdoll, but can be timed while the opponent is in the air. An inconsistent move it can combo after is the jump variant of Turbulence, as timing the hit can extend the duration the opponent is in the air (Stalling her own cooldowns, or leading into a few extra hits with Thin Ice Breaker). If she's in Sky Veil, she can try to catch her opponent off guard by using the aerial version of Sky Distortion, giving Sky Bender mobility towards her opponent, in case of a blunder from them (front dashing away, using move to predict where she is, etc.)

Close up, temper Sky Distortion can deal out a whopping 15 damage! But unlike its normal variant, temper Sky Distortion can turn into a ranged blockbreaker! Using it while on the ground picks up debris, and adds an additional 5 damage because the debris is being picked up, making it deal 10 damage (If used as a projectile). This projectile will only happen if the opponent is far enough to where the melee hit does not register as an actual hit. If the bullet lands on the opponent who is close, they will be launched away from Sky Bender. But if the bullet lands on an opponent who is far, they will be flung TOWARDS the opposite direction the move hits them from, launching them closer to Sky Bender. If temper Sky Distortion hits someone directly above them (who is not ragdolled), they will throw them up into the air instead, allowing to chain all four of your air m1s from the boost temper gives Sky Bender, since it launches the opponent high enough to initiate the command. If Sky Bender's opponent is ragdolled and [b][u]IN THE SKY[/u][/b], they can use temper Sky Distortion to make the move become an auto-targeting bullet that will, unless the opponent uses evasive, hit the enemy no matter the direction Sky Bender is facing. The only thing that stops the bullet is a wall. When the bullet lands, it performs the same mechanics as what the normal variant does, launching the opponent away if Sky Bender is too close, or towards the opposite direction it hits them from afar. If used properly, it can lead to another set of air m1s on the opponent.

Sky Veil is a straight forward skill. Sky Bender shrouds herself via Sky Manipulation, and goes invisible to the naked eye. She moves around with increased speed for 2 seconds, and pressing any keybind set to a move allows her to use that move while invisible, unshrouding herself and using the move simultaneously. while she is invisible, she cannot m1 or dash (any direction), and is limited to walking with increased speed. She is able to jump. If the 2 seconds run out, or if R is clicked again, Sky Bender will unveil herself, and don't be able to use moves for a VERY small duration.

Sky Bender's combos might be considered "low damage" in her base kit because of how many Blue Sparks her combos add. Although she may cause their opponent to gain evasive quickly, this factor does NOT take away any of the Megumi (potential) she has. Be smart, and combo wisely!

Sky Bender's aerial m1, when in temper mode, has [b]no required[/b] action needed in order to trigger it, allowing her to punish targets who use certain movement tools. Some examples are high wall jumps, or Restless Gambler's Shutter Door bounce. Sky Bender using her superior air mobility to punish Restless Gambler. UroRender:PIPTA
After doing 3 M1s and then an uppercut surf on her opponent, using aerial Sky Distortion will allow Sky Bender to do the aimable version of Thin Ice Breaker which allows her to get an air M1 in.

After using Blind Rage and aiming her camera up in the last few seconds of flight, Sky Bender can cause the enemy to be flung upwards into her, where she can then M1 into an air M1 before side dashing directly after for a third air M1.

If a move on cooldown is used during Sky Veil, it will perform a version where she has no exit lag, which allows her to sneak up on your opponent for an unreactable m1/side dash (Leave them guessing where she could be with some mind games).

When using grounded Turbulence, aiming backwards then shiftlocking forwards will make the hit box reappear in front of her without visuals too the enemy. (Do know it is still blockable and Sky Bender can't hit around block with it)
By uppercutting her opponent and using Sky Distortion afterwards, Sky Bender is able to hold down her m1s for an aerial m1 into another uppercut!

Honored One is the "average", not really failing in any categories while not excelling in any either, but against Sky Bender, that changes. Honored One can easily counter Sky Bender's moves by being able to teleport. Surprisingly, this counters most of Sky Bender's moves. Turbulence? Teleport. Thin Ice Breaker whiff? Teleport (then again, Sky Bender shouldn't be using Thin Ice Breaker in neutral anyways). Sky Bender has less time to catch Honored One off guard with Sky Veil because of Honored One's first m1 being slightly faster (if predicted), which does slightly hinder Sky Bender if she's trying to use Dark Mango Psychology (Please check [url=https://dogslamloop.com/characters/Sky_bender/index.html#sec-dark-mango-psychology]here[multicolor=#ef4444,#3b82f6][/multicolor][/url] to know what is being said) to get a few quick m1s in. If there is one thing Honored One does the best, it's m1 trading. What truly makes Sky Veil risky to use would be Honored One's 2+R variant, where using it during an opponent's move freezes them in place. Since Sky Veil lasts a whopping two seconds, Honored One has ≤ 2 seconds to simply click two buttons to interrupt Sky Bender.

Vessel is more annoying than he is difficult to deal with. Vessel doesn't leap high enough when using their feints for mobility, so Sky Bender can't punish them. Even if she tries to catch them off guard with Turbulence, Vessel gets just high enough to leap over the move, rendering it useless in neutral. Vessel's m1s are faster, so m1 trading with Vessel is rigged in their favor, unless they fail to read a side dash. Punishing Vessel isn't really an option, and Sky Bender has better odds by just focusing on combos after a successful m1 trade instead. When m1 trading — or when an opponent uses any move in general — Manji Kick is Vessel's best friend! This is especially the case for Sky Bender as most of Sky Bender's moves are parryable. The only move that isn't parryable is Turbulence, plus all of its variants (the jump variant of Turbulence is semi-parryable, as its damage changes from melee to explosion). Sky Bender's best bet would be to try and predict when Vessel will strike, and bait out their Manji Kick, as that's all they really have going for them.

The one thing that makes Sky Bender powerful against her opponents is the ability to throw back projectiles and shut down any aerial advances. Restless Gambler is a prime example of this! If Restless Gambler wants an unblockable variant to their aerial Rough Energy, they have to use Shutter Doors in order to reach enough height in the air. Luckily for Sky Bender, it simply doesn't matter whether or not Restless Gambler bounces on Shutter Doors while she's in temper! If they do choose to bounce, Sky Bender can hold down her m1s to instantly shut down the move, leading to [b][u]TWO[/u][/b] of Restless Gambler's moves being on cooldown, while Sky Bender didn't have to waste anything in order to land a hit! This is because like some of the other character's moves (Like Honored One's lapse blue + 2, or Head of the Hei's variant for Decisive Strike if his opponent is high enough in the air), Sky Bender's m1s focus on distance from the ground! So, by Restless Gambler using Shutter Doors and bouncing on them, they doom themselves into wasting two moves if Sky Bender has temper! Shutter Door plus Reserve Balls is always a good combo starter when it comes to Restless Gambler, but Sky Bender can take that for themselves! Sky Distortion reflects any projectiles and hits the opponent with them! Even some bigger entities, like Open and Hollow Purple, can get reflected! Although they will most likely kill Sky Bender in the process. This mechanic allows Sky Bender to reflect the variant, causing Restless Gambler if caught off guard, to be hit by their own move! The only real threats are if Sky Bender wastes evasive early, since Restless Gambler's parry will be used to maximize damage, as Sky Bender shut down most of their moves. If Sky Bender thinks Restless Gambler is going to parry, she can use the jump variant of Turbulence without hitting the initial kick so that the parry has time to go away, so she can punish Restless Gambler.

If Sky Bender gets hit down because of evasive being used in the sky (AKA Sky Bender whiffing the punch and being set with major endlag, causing the punch to land instead of being blocked), it'll knock Sky Bender down into a move. This doesn't seem like a problem at first, but keep in mind that Ten Shadows is able to hit ragdoll with every move, meaning Sky Bender's blunder can cause her to be caught in a combo from Ten Shadows, or at the LEAST an m1 chain after Ten Shadows uses Toad. Ten Shadows is good at zoning Sky Bender, but can also cancel Sky Bender out of any move with their [u][b]TOAD[/b][/u]. Toad can pick Sky Bender up for an easy m1 chain. Every move is punishable by toad if Sky Bender whiffs; [i]EVERY MOVE.[/i] If Sky Bender uses temper, Ten Shadows can use Toad. If Sky Bender manages to get temper off, any move can also be cancelled if used in neutral. [i]Sky Bender has to rely on combos in order to win.[/i] If she is even caught using a move in neutral, Toad will punish Sky Bender. Along with having to combo, if Ten Shadows evasives in the middle of Sky Bender's combo, since she doesn't have any moves that have true ragdoll, Ten Shadows can punish Sky Bender. Sky Bender relies on precise and high damage combos in a short amount of time, and anything that kills that flow during the combo can put an end to Sky Bender.

Sky Bender's worst enemy is [color=#fff8f8]Rika[/color] when fighting Cursed Partners, as Sky Veil is obsolete if [color=#fff8f8]Rika[/color]'s moves are back. Turbulence's ground variant in Sky Veil does [b][i]NOT[/i][/b] counter any [color=#fff8f8]Rika[/color] moves, so Sky Bender's best option is to either not use Sky Veil at all, or wait until Rika's moves are used. Cursed Partners can keep Sky Bender at a distance while dishing out constant damage from combos that will chip down Sky Bender's health FAST. If Sky Bender can close the distance between her and the Cursed Partners, she might be able to put in some good damage against the Cursed Partners. Sky Bender should take advantage of if Cursed Partners uses Outburst, as she doesn't want Cursed Partners to capitalize off of a blunder from her two blockable moves that have a lot of endlag on whiff/block. [i][b] SKY BENDER NEEDS TO BE SURE TO PREDICT EVASIVE AFTER BLIND RAGE[/b][/i], as Cursed Partners can easily capitalize off of ragdolled opponents.
"You Fujiwara are always in my way! Are you that afraid of me becoming somebody?!"

Sky Bender's going to wish that her moves weren't close ranged when she's done fighting Disaster Plants! considering every move has long endlag if whiffed, or is blockable if far ranged, she's about as strong as a Gazelle is when fighting a Lion. What's that? Gazelles don't fight Lions, they run? That's exactly Sky Bender's plan! This is one of the only times that the close range character [b][u]CANNOT[/u][/b] play aggressively. Sky Bender NEEDS to play passively, so her best bets are to: Pray Disaster Plants messes up Surging Thorns in neutral, so she can immediately use Blind Rage Pray Disaster Plants gets distracted while using their R variants, so she can immediately use Blind Rage Pray Disaster Plants isn't in a flower field, so she can immediately use Blind Rage Pray Disaster Plants gets hit enough to let her temper meter get high, so she can immediately use temper Blind Rage The whole match relies on the only semi-reliable blockbreaker, Blind Rage. Blind Rage, since applying pressure with any other move will get Sky Bender stuck in a combo, helps her damage Disaster Plants! This damage can eventually (with a LOT of time) build up enough meter to use temper, which will let Sky Bender finally have an unblockable move that can hit Disaster Plants without being [i]as[/i] at risk of being full comboed! ...hopefully.

Granite blast or Appetizer?: Jump variant of Sky Distortion ([kbd]2[/kbd]) to close the gap while dealing extra damage! Holding Granite Blast?: Use Turbulence ([kbd]3[/kbd]) to cancel the move while launching True Cannon towards her! True Cannon names a move, and Sky Bender will have a solution! With the help of their amazing "I hate True Cannon" kit, True Cannon becomes a near non-lethal threat for once! To counter his melee attacks like Second Helping and Unsatisfied, Sky Bender [i]could[/i] use Sky Veil ([kbd]R[/kbd]) and instantly use Turbulence for the parry variant, but the most optimal route would be to simply avoid them, and then counter attack with the ground version of Turbulence if she try to gain distance. If Sky Bender wants to be stylish, she can use the jump variant of Turbulence to hover above a Granite Blast from True Cannon to get an easy hit, which will be easier if the True Cannon is panicking. The only advantage True Cannon has on Sky Bender is that if she uses aerial 3, he can SOMETIMES punish her with Second Helping, but it is not useful as a neutral option in this case, as Sky Bender has more than enough tools to stop his advances.

This is one of the only matchups that is really equal for Sky Bender. Both Lucky Coward and Sky Bender have to be careful in this match! If Sky Bender is dodged, Lucky Coward can use the endlag to get a few moves off on Sky Bender, plus a miracle. On the opposite end, if Lucky Coward wastes evasive, Sky Bender can get them to red, and sometimes even get rid of a bar of miracles! In the end, it all boils down to who is going to play more aggressively, and who will capitalize off of a blunder. Both characters are able to deal with each other relatively easy.

No matter what Sky Bender presses, Black Death will always have the upper hand. Anything Sky Bender does can and WILL get countered, even if it's unintentional. Sky Veil, just like Sky Bender's matchup with Cursed Partners, is also rendered useless. If Black Death uses Earthen Insect Trance ([kbd]R[/kbd]) right before Sky Bender uses Sky Veil, Black Death will constantly know where she is. That, along with the short stun it gives, that can cancel heavy moves like Blind Rage, and allow Black Death to get the upper hand on Sky Bender. If Black Death does not use Earthen Insect Trance, Injuries apply a faint glow each tick it hits, allowing for further shutdown of Sky Veil. Beyond Sky Veil, Black Death also can outrange Sky Bender. Yes, detach is parryable via Sky Distortion, but Festering Strikes makes most close range moves useless, as it naturally parries, and Black Death's kit is already strong on its own, so thinks such as Sky Distortion and Thin Ice Breaker get flung off without any real punishment to Black death. Overall, the matchup will NOT go well.

Pretty self explanatory, the [color=hsl(275, 17%, 60%)]Sky Benders[/color] will be in a fight that'll have more time in the air than on the ground. The match will be based on who has better knowledge of both Jujutsu Shenanigans and Sky Bender.
There's no hope. forget trying to win, run for your life.

Star Rage is an M1 Merchant reliant on true and safe combos due to having no evasive bait. She has extremely moderate neutral control with [i]Garuda Stab Variant[/i] being on a 20s cooldown and only one safe follow-up, that being [i]Garuda Rebound[/i]. Star Rage can dish out extremely high damage combos when their opponents use their evasive, and can still be fully viable if her opponent never uses their evasive. Star Rage is known for extremely high damage, "techy" combos that require a higher level of mechanical skill and game sense than other characters. Most of her moves do not hit on grounded ragdoll, making using her moves on getup a common playstyle. Her safe/true ragdoll combos require difficult timings, and combining this with her high endlag on her skills makes mistiming and other mistakes extremely critical and guarantees you to be punished by your opponent. When Star Rage is played appropriately to her full potential, she is extremely deadly and will outclass other M1 Merchant archetypes.

Star Rage has little to no consistent way to bait evasive - a majority of her moves lack the pressure to choke out an evasive as other moves would. For instance, Garuda Stab's R variant struggles to bait evasive as it doesn't have many high damage, threatening, and safe conversions. Garuda Stab R into Garuda Rebound is the safest guaranteed conversion off of Garuda Stab R Garuda Stab R into Rising Rage on getup requires excellent timing and is evasive punishable if expected Garuda Stab R in Mass Breaker can be easily reacted to and punished with evasive
Keep your distance after Garuda Stab R to make sure you can't be evasive punished. M1 M1 M1 GARUDA STAB (R) GARUDA REBOUND FIRST USE GARUDA REBOUND SECOND USE
M1 Start Garuda Stab Safe Combo
Garuda Stab (R) Garuda Rebound First Use Garuda Rebound Second Use
Garuda Stab R Start Safe Combo

Star Rage's Neutral is dependent on Garuda Stab R to engage without an m1 trade, and rarely mass breaker to finish someone off if they waste side dash. When Garuda Stab R is on cooldown, Star Rage will be left with just M1s to engage. Garuda Stab R Variant heavily carries Star Rage's neutral game in her kit - it has extremely long range, does 21 damage, and is unblockable. It also has low endlag, and places her safely in the air where she cannot be punished. It is an amazing way to engage and also her only viable option in neutral. Garuda Rebound's second use can allow the Star Rage to engage safely, as the second use cancels Front Dashes, M1s and blocking. If the opponent tries to Block the Front Dash or Side Dash M1, they won't be able to parry the secound use of Garuda Rebound, letting the Star Rage do chip damage. If the Star Rage manages to hit the Front Dash they can simply aim Garuda Rebound away and continue using M1s. The only viable strategy for the opponent is to back off and avoid getting hit by Garuda Rebound's second use. Mass Breaker in neutral can only be viable if her opponent wastes their sidedash, as the long windup and endlag allows them to easily react and punish. This is only good for chip damage, and is more optimal to be saved for combos. Garuda Rebound is extremely reactable and the parry window is very lenient. When Star Rage tries to parry back, often she is too close and still in endlag from the second use, or the parry will pass through her and not go back to her opponent. Parrying is very inconsistent and also has no safe conversions. Base Garuda Stab can act similarly to Honored One's Rapid Punches in M1 trades as it is an unblockable grab and can grab from longer range than M1s.

As stated, these are simpler as they are less executionally demanding than the techier ones. Simple Bread and Butter combo to safely convert off ragdoll and hit. Only costs you two moves. Do NOT extend with Mass Breaker R - not worth less damage and mass, instead use base Mass Breaker on get up M1 M1 M1 UPPERCUT GARUDA REBOUND ONCE GARUDA REBOUND TWICE GARUDA STAB OR RISING RAGE Higher damage BNB that leaves you with Garuda Stab and drains 2/3 of your mass meter. M1 M1 M1 UPPERCUT GARUDA REBOUND ONCE GARUDA REBOUND TWICE RISING RAGE (Rx2) MASS BREAKER Similar to previous but opens with rising rage. Leaves you with mass breaker in neutral. M1 M1 M1 UPPERCUT RISING RAGE GARUDA REBOUND ONCE GARUDA REBOUND TWICE GARUDA STAB

These combos employ techs and are where Star Rage starts to see her infamous high combo damage output. Use Garuda Rebound's slow variant to use the 2nd hit to cancel the CD of rising rage and get a second use. Use sidedash to land second rising rage if 2nd rebound use not aimed to knock back the opponent to you. COSTS NO MASS AND ONLY USES TWO MOVES. M1 M1 M1 UPPERCUT GARUDA REBOUND (SLOWED) ONCE RISING RAGE OR MASS BREAKER GARUDA REBOUND TWICE RISING RAGE OR MASS BREAKER (pick the one you used to CD cancel initially) M1 reset with Rising Rage RX2, cancelling its animation to let you use base Rising Rage again. Costs just TWO MOVES. M1 M1 M1 UPPERCUT GARUDA REBOUND (SLOWED) ONCE RISING RAGE (RX2) GARUDA REBOUND TWICE (AIMED AWAY TO WHIFF) FRONTDASH M1 M1 M1 UPPERCUT RISING RAGE Difficult to land, but with practise is a very safe hard to punish combo. The traditional home run combo. M1 M1 M1 UPPERCUT TURN AROUND AND GARUDA REBOUND (SLOWED) ONCE TURN BACK AROUND AND GARUDA STAB R VARIANT GARUDA REBOUND TWICE WHILE IN AIR TURN AROUND AND MASS BREAKER TO HIT OPPONENT IN AIR Requires a ton of execution while being the highest damage combo - you must perform a rising rage cd cancel and land rising rage on getup twice, land mass breaker on get up AND charge mass meter mid combo. M1 M1 M1 UPPERCUT GARUDA STAB R GARUDA REBOUND ONCE RISING RAGE GARUDA REBOUND TWICE CHARGE MASS METER RISING RAGE RX2 MASS BREAKER Requires you to have a full mass bar, but is less executionally demanding while still being a pretty safe conversion save for the mass breaker R. On the brightside, that makes it fully RED and UNCOUNTERABLE. M1 M1 M1 UPPERCUT RISING RAGE MASS BREAKER R GARUDA REBOUND ONCE GARUDA REBOUND TWICE GARUDA STAB R VARIANT BASICALLY, Star Rage's main way of converting into those advanced combos is either off an m1 trade win or using getup tech to land her moves on the opponent's ragdoll off a stray hit like Garuda Stab R or Mass Breaker base.

Star Rage's shikigami curls up into a ball before getting launched straight forward with a kick. After reaching the maximum distance or hitting an enemy, the shikigami will rebound upwards and back towards Star Rage. By holding the skill rather than tapping it, the speed of the shikigami's rebound will reduce drastically, allowing Star Rage to prepare other attacks or mix up the enemy. Both Garuda Rebound I and II are able to track airborne enemies, so if Star Rage was to use the skill after hitting an enemy with Rising Rage, both uses of the skill will be able to target the enemy in the air.

By using Garuda Rebound again [b]right when the shikigami reaches her[/b], Star Rage will punch the shikigami with great force, having it fly forward until it reaches its maximum distance or hits an enemy. Contrary to Garuda Rebound I, this attack is unblockable, and will [b]send the enemy towards Star Rage[/b] rather than knocking them away. However, Garuda Rebound II [b]can be parried[/b] by the enemy. If they quickly block right when the shikigami is about to slam into them, the shikigami will be sent back towards Star Rage, hitting her instead and sending her towards the enemy unless she parries the parried shikigami, which will again send it back to the enemy. [b]Garuda Rebound II can also be cancelled into while Star Rage is using any other skill.[/b] For instance, she can kick the shikigami, use Mass Breaker, and then punch the shikigami once it comes back and it will immediately cut off the endlag for the move and fire the shikigami again. This tech is where the majority of Star Rage's skill expression comes in, and will be gone over much more in the Techs and Combos pages. Using Garuda Rebound II will put the move on a longer, 20s cooldown rather than Garuda Rebound I's 14s cooldown.

With a full mass meter, Star Rage can use their special after initially kicking the shikigami to imbue mass within it. This will grant her an [b]automatic[/b] kick follow-up once it comes back to her, kicking it a second time and propelling it forward with incredible force. This projectile will deal increased damage, but instead of bringing the enemy toward Star Rage, it will launch them away. Similarly to Garuda Rebound II, [b]this attack can be parried[/b] (albeit it's a little more difficult), and will launch Star Rage away if she does not parry it back. The shikigami also gains ricochet properties, bouncing off of walls repeatedly until it comes in contact with an enemy or it does not hit an enemy for a few seconds. Like Garuda Rebound II, any other skill can be cancelled into the kick. There is a rare and random chance that a Blue Lock voice line will play upon Star Rage kicking the shikigami a second time. This does [b]not[/b] change the properties of the move itself.

Star Rage, imbuing their legs with cursed energy, sweeps and launches enemies in front of her. The second kick sends enemies flying up in the air. The base version of this move is blockable, interruptible, and only hits a ragdolled enemy on the second hit, so Star Rage must ensure she is using it in its most optimal situation if it is not imbued with mass.

By using her special once after beginning the Rising Rage animation, Star Rage will both nullify the launch properties of the second kick, and will add a third, powerful kick to the end of the sequence that will bludgeon the enemy and send them tumbling to the side. This third kick will afflict the enemy with multiple debuffs for a few seconds, being a red blur on their screen and ringing in their ears. The potency of this debuff is indicated by how red the enemy is after being hit by the third kick.

By using her special twice once the animation for Rising Rage begins, Star Rage will add on two additional hits in the kick sequence. The third kick is the same as Mass-Imbued Rising Rage I, but does not knock them away or inflict any debuffs, and will instead make them slide a small distance forward on the ground, stunning them for a second. After the third kick, Star Rage will remain still for a moment, imbuing a great amount of mass into her right leg before propelling herself forward and crushing the enemy in the chest. This final kick has many additional properties: Unblockable Uncounterable Inflicts True Ragdoll Deals Explosion Damage Cannot Kill the Enemy

Star Rage winds her arm back with noticeable startup before lunging forward a set distance before punching the enemy in the chest and firing them away. The direction of the move can be adjusted before she propels herself. There is also an airborne variant that works fundamentally the same as the standard skill, but allows Star Rage to aim upwards or downwards as well.

Having the same windup animation, Star Rage will instead spin in the air before crashing into the enemy. This buffed skill allows Mass Breaker to hit grounded ragdolled enemies. The skill is also uncounterable, like Mass-Imbued Star Rage II's final kick, dealing explosion damage. Finally, the smash will send the enemies at a more upwards angle rather than straight forwards. Notably, the mass-imbued variant deals less damage than the former standard Mass Breaker.

Star Rage takes hold of her shikigami, pulling it back before having it thrust forward, piercing any enemy in front of her. The stab is unblockable and, if it connects, Star Rage herself follows up with a downwards kick that send the enemy upwards in the air.

Using their special after executing the skill, Star Rage throws their shikigami forward before it attempts to stab an enemy, granting it staggeringly more range. After it stabs someone, it will reel them back towards Star Rage who kicks the enemy to the ground, bouncing herself up and triggering a final slam down by whipping her shikigami down at the enemy. This variant is arguably Star Rage's most powerful neutral tool, being very fast, having exceptional range and allowing her to follow up with Garuda Rebound, leading to damaging combos.

By holding down R, Star Rage will drain her awakening meter in exchange for a mass reserve, as shown besides her character. She also pulses purple when starting to charge mass, and there are sound cues as well. However, enemies cannot see the meter when it is being charged. By having mass accumulated, this reserve can be consumed to enhance her base skills: [b]Garuda Rebound[/b] | 100% Mass Cost | [i]Increased Damage & Knockback[/i] [b]Rising Rage I[/b] | 30% Mass Cost | [i]Increased Damage & Debuff Affliction[/i] [b]Rising Rage II[/b] | 60% Mass Cost | [i]Increased Damage, Uncounterable[/i] [b]Mass Breaker[/b] | 30% Mass Cost | [i]Ragdoll Hit Properties, Uncounterable[/i] [b]Garuda Stab[/b] | 50% Mass Cost | [i]Increased Damage, Massively Increased Range[/i] Managing this meter well is the cornerstone of Star Rage's entire game plan. Knowing when not to spend mass on moves is arguably just as important as knowing when to spend mass.

Star Rage uses skill and hits her opponent the moment they stand up from ragdoll. If timed correctly, it is completely red and uncounterable. This allows her to extend her combo off ragdoll with moves that don't hit grounded ragdoll.

Allows Star Rage to combo extend with Rising Rage for a risky high damage true combo, or a safe combo with Garuda Stab R. m1 m1 jump m1 (in the air) mass breaker Rising rage / garuda rebound / garuda stab

Allows Star Rage to use the same move twice in one combo by canceling a moves animation and refunding the cooldown. Garuda rebound first use rising rage / mass breaker (any variant) garuda rebound second use

Gives Star Rage an M1 reset at the cost of only Garuda Rebound. Rising Rage is refunded and can be used again. This can be implemented into a combo after Garuda Stab R, but is very risky and conditional. Downslam Garuda REbound first use, hold variant rising rage rx1 (on getup) garuda rebound second use m1 m1 m1

Gives Star Rage an M1 reset at the cost of only Garuda Rebound. Rising Rage is refunded and can be used again. This version of the reset does not require getup, making it more consistent. uppercut garuda rebound first use, hold variant (instantly, walking forward to position under them) jump (when rebound comes out) rising rage rx1 (first kick hits opponent when they are coming down) Garuda rebound second use m1 m1 m1

Gives Star Rage an M1 reset at the cost of only Garuda Rebound. Rising Rage is refunded and can be used again, and is the easiest M1 Reset in her kit. uppercut garuda rebound first use, hold variant rising rage rx2 (instant) garuda rebound second use Forward dash (optional) m1 m1 m1
Gives Star Rage a high damage combo option with similar damage to one of the Rising Rage M1 resets. Use case is when Rising Rage is on cooldown and the opponent does not have evasive.

Very situational option that can come in handy if conditions are met. Star Rage must have full Mass Buildup bar, only Garuda Rebound off cooldown, and opponent must not have evasive. Usually done for style. uppercut garuda rebound first use (instantly, walkijng forward to position under them) Jump (when rebound comes out) R (as soon as rebound hits them) garuda rebound R (no input)

A part of Rising Rage Rx1 m1 Reset (Uppercut) and Garuda Rebound Uppercut Confirm to be possible by launching her opponent higher than usual. Timing is very difficult and ping must be accounted for as the timing changes slightly. Uppercut Garuda rebound first use (instantly, walking forward to position under them) Jump (when rebound comes out)
You must go to [url=#sec-technical-overview]Technical Overview[/url] and understand Garuda Rebound to its full extent.

No strange interactions between moves, but Honored One's ability to pressure her Mass Buildup with his Limitless can force her to cancel her charge. This can greatly reduce your combo potential if Honored One has good usage of Limitless.

Vessel's Manji Kick can counter all of Star Rage's moves besides Mass Breaker R. If Star Rage has any green in her combos, which is very common with using moves on getup, Vessel can get out of combos for free. Be very mindful of Vessel's counter and attempt to bait it by faking ability usage on getup. If she uses Garuda Stab R in neutral predictably, Vessel can counter it. Use Garuda Stab R more unpredictably to avoid this. If timed right, Aerial Cursed Strikes can punish Garuda Stab Variant consistently, making using the move risky.
Similarly, to Vessel's matchup, Restless Gambler has a counter at his disposal to punish any green in combos. Once again, Star Rage should be very mindful of his counter usage and baiting it out.

Star Rage has an easy time getting rid of Ten Shadows' Divine Dog: Totality. Garuda Stab Variant and Mass Breaker after her opponent has used side dash can ragdoll Ten Shadows and take Divine Dog: Totality out of the picture.

Blood Manipulator destroys Star Rage overall in neutral with his Supernova. Garuda Stab Variant can be used to get rid of Supernova orbs, or to pull Blood Manipulator away from a Aerial Flowing Red Scale orb he is camping, but the cooldown of Garuda Stab Variant is too long for this to be a lasting strategy.
If Switcher uses swap a lot in neutral, it can often cause Star Rage to miss Garuda Stab Variant, her only viable neutral.
Defense Attorney can evasive as soon as possible after being hit by Garuda Stab Variant to use Grapple. This allows him to guaranteed combo start.

Cursed Partners has many tools at his disposal against Star Rage's combos. Outburst Parry is extremely good at getting out of green combos, and can lead to a red punish depending on the move that was parried. Cursed Partners also has Rika, which he can mash one of her moves if he is in a combo. If the combo is green for even a moment, Rika becomes actionable and can get him out of the combo. Star Rage must be EXTREMELY mindful of these interactions, and may have to change up her playstyle to bait out Outburst Parry and Rika.
No notable interactions, Puppet Master overall neutral, safety, and combo diffs Star Rage.

Head of the Hei can safely use Decisive Strikes Aerial by using evasive as soon as possible after being hit by Star Rage's Garuda Stab Variant. Star Rage can block it, but is still safe for Head of the Hei most of the time. Star Rage has a difficult time using Garuda Stab Variant or using Mass Breaker (after baiting side dash) in neutral due to Head of Hei having two side dashes. This overall makes her moves even less viable than they already are in neutral.

True Cannon can evasive as soon as possible after being hit by Garuda Stab Variant to use Granite Blast to combo start. True Cannon also has insane pressure on Star Rage's Mass Buildup, making it difficult for her to find a time to charge.
Star Rage can pressure Star Rage's Mass buildup with Garuda Rebound and Garuda Stab Variant. While Star Rage can pressure Star Rage's Mass buildup with Garuda Rebound and Garuda Stab Variant.

Star Rage is often forced to play like an M1 merchant, and this matchup absoluetly cripples her. Aspiring Mangaka can counter all of Star Rages Neutral, and can mash counter in moments where he knows the combo can be green, and can do it as much as he wants until he misses it. Aspiring Mangaka also has Oracle to perfect block in M1 trades, and perfect block Rising Rage getup, making it even easier to punish, as if it wasn't already a guaranteed punish on block. Worst of all, Aspiring Mangaka's Clairvoyance gives him and insane advantage in M1 trades against an already completely crippled Star Rage. To top it all off, Clairvoyance: Prediction CANCELS Mass Buildup, and as long as Aspiring Mangaka Successfully keeps Clairvoyance on Star Rage, she can virtually never charge her Mass. This can be considered to be the worst matchup in the game.

Lucky Coward can dodge Garuda Stab Variant easily in sword off mode, and Star Rage has no viable means of catching up to a passive Lucky Coward in sword off. If Star Rage can catch him, its easy for him to dodge green parts of combos and farm miracles. Lucky Coward's multiple evasives make high damage combos very rare as well. Even if she catches him without evasive while in sword off, all of Star Rage's high damage combos and reset and easily cancelable by Ankle Cutter and High Time. Star Rage should depend on safe and true combos.

Crow Charmer overall out neutrals Star Rage and has many more engagement tools. Garuda Stab Variant is also less viable as Crow Charmer can easily use Spatial Transference to teleport over the move, but may still get hit by the other hits of the move.

Black Death can pressure Star Rage's Mass Buildup with detach and roach swarm, giving her less opportunities to use variants. Black Death overall also outranges Star Rage, making spacing for Garuda Stab Variant actually work in favor of Black Death.

Upon death and using her ultimate, Star Rage screams and makes a last-ditch effort to grab onto anyone nearby. If this dash is missed, Star Rage will die unceremoniously. However, if Star Rage does grab onto the enemy, she is prompted to begin charging her special. Imbuing extreme amounts of mass onto herself, collapsing space so much so that not even light can escape, forming a black hole. Upon the black hole completely forming, her and the enemy she is latched on to will be devoured by it, dying instantly. It will also form a massive gravitational pull zone around it, making any other enemy within this zone be brought towards it. Anyone in this zone will also take increments of damage, a maximum of about 28.5 per tick, which decreases the farther away you are from the black hole. All skills and M1s are disabled for the duration of the black hole for anyone that is within its range. After a few seconds, the black hole will collapse onto itself, vanishing into thin air. This is... uh... the worst awakening in the game. Bar none. It is only usable on death, can only guarantee the death of one person, and still kills Star Rage no matter what happens. It also uses her entire awakening meter, which is the cornerstore of Star Rage's entire game plan.
So you can kinda do this and that, very awesome

Intentionally overpowered boss character that can utterly curbstomp any of the vanilla cast in a 1v1. However, Heian Sukuna isn't playable outside of private/custom servers with Overpowered turned on and Final Showdown, meaning that in most cases, you'll be dealing with entire crowds as opposed to single targets. *Health scales with amount of players in Roulette server.

At a basic level Strongest of History can really just use any move over and over again mindlessly besides Open Furnace and get results, but the Strongest of History should be trying to make distance to use certain moves and build up his incantations.

Whenever possible, Strongest of History wants to use his R special to build up his incantations. Any of Strongest of History's incantation-boosted Strong Dismantles are usable, but the most viable ones typically go like this from strongest to weakest. Dismantle Net -> Dismantle Barrage -> World Cutting Slash -> Disgraced Sovereign Dismantle Net is even stronger than Open Furnace in lethality, so Strongest of History can use Cleave Rush to space himself and then fire it with no consequences. Dismantle Barrage is a great tool to space himself as well, and does great damage of course. It can be led into an Open Furnace or Dismantle Net with minimal risk. World Cutting Slash is similar to Dismantle net, although due to its much more minimized range and requiring Strongest of History to aim, it will be less viable in more situations, though if the Strongest of History is skilled it is basically interchangable with Dismantle Barrage. Disgraced Sovereign due to its low damage output and pitiful AOE (for a character like Strongest of History) is not as good as the other incantation-boosted Dismantles. In most cases, you are better off using Dismantle Barrage. But it does look cool, so that's something it has going for it.

Strongest of History has a black flash variant within Cleave Rush that is easily timeable. Keep note that after Black Flashing you have little to no endlag, which does provide Strongest of History with an ounce of combo game, if you want to take out important targets.

Switcher is a character revolving around his burst damage and his swaps. With most of his moves being close range, he's sure to do a lot of damage if an opponent lets him win an engagement, with tools in his disposal to get in their face and start fighting. [color=hsl(180, 100%, 83%)]Boogie Woogie[/color] is his special which can act as a way to dodge, disorient, and feint, but is best used as a catalyst for his variants. He has Swift Kick, which is a kick that comes out moderately fast into a grab that can extend his combos. His third move, Pebble Throw, is a versatile tool that's used best with his special, acting as both an approach tool and a combo extender into a move with high burst damage, like Brute Force. With the combination of his newfound combo potential, as well as an effective approach tool and evasive bait, Switcher is one hard-hitting pick for a character that mostly relies on fundamentals.[color=hsl(180, 100%, 83%)][/color]

Switcher's gameplan is to get up close using [i]Pebble Throw[/i], with its two variants: [i]Blazing Star[/i] is the move that allows Switcher to glide around his opponent, letting him hit different angles fast. [i]Gut Punch[/i] is [i]Pebble Throw's[/i] second variant, which either directly puts him in an advantageous position, stunning his opponent and swapping him in front of them, or in a neutral position favored towards him if its blocked due to its low endlag. It's a high priority for Switcher to bait out evasive, as most of his moves have high enough startup to be easily punishable, which can be done with [i]Swift Kick[/i] and [s](again)[/s] [i]Pebble Throw[/i], as [i]Pebble Throw[/i] threatens a 30 damage followup.

The defining trait of Switcher that differentiates him from other characters. Boogie Woogie, with its very low startup up close, can be unpredictable against an opponent during an M1 trade, forcing them to constantly react to his swaps. It also can feint moves at any point during them, allowing him to mitigate his high whiff endlag on his moves, as well as to keep combos true, namely with [i]Elbow Drop[/i]. These are other uses for [color=hsl(180, 100%, 83%)]Boogie Woogie[/color]: Feint mixups Combo extending after using [i]Brute Force[/i] Swapping himself or his opponent to an object made by an opponent (Lucky Coward's sword, Black Death's Earthen Insect Trance, etc.)

He can use Blazing Star, Pebble Throw's variant, to get close with his opponent. Pebble Throw can also be a good interruption tool, with its low startup and its follow-up to Gut punch. He can also use Boogie Woogie during M1 trades, in tandem with sidedashes, to gain a positional advantage. If an opponent burnt their sidedash within sidedash range, he can use sidedash and Elbow Drop as it's unblockable.

Switcher kicks his opponent, dealing 9 damage and knocking them away standing up, then goes for a grab and throws them away, dealing 1 and 9 damage respectively. His kick's startup is fast, but slow enough to be reactable after 4 M1s, with his grab coming out relatively fast after landing the kick, usually guaranteeing you hit the grab after the kick. His grab can also be aimed from straight up to straight down, opening for a lot of unique combos.

Switcher starts sliding straight into the opponent, dealing 7.5 damage. The Switcher then follows up with a kick straight up on the opponent, dealing 7.5 damage. The move has a fast startup, but it comes at the cost of being unsteerable during the kick. Switcher, during the slide, is in a ragdolled state, and can only be hit by moves that hit ragdoll and still has melee and bullet invincibility for whole active hitbox. If the opponent is ragdolled, the kick will not go into the second followup attack and instead keep travelling forward after the slide connects.

Switcher winds up for a moment before delivering a devastating punch, dealing 17.5 damage. The punch comes out with enough force for the wind gust to blow the opponent away if they're not close enough, dealing 6 damage. The move has a slow startup, with moderate whiff endlag.

During Blazing Star, Switcher can use Brute Force to wind up a devastating kick, essentially doing the same thing as base Brute Force. However, if Brute Force is pressed again with correct timing, Switcher can hit a black flash, dealing 24 damage and knocking them away.

Switcher kicks up and punches a pebble, dealing 4 damage if it hits an opponent, the hit is true stunning for 0.45s and get up ragdolls, lingers for 1.5 seconds if whiffed. This move's utility comes from what Switcher can do after throwing the pebble, being able to swap with the pebble for movement, or to swap in front of his opponent to attack them. This move has relatively high startup, with options right after using it.

Switcher charges up an uppercut, dealing 5 damage, before slamming down on their opponent with their elbow, bouncing them up [s]sometimes[/s] and dealing 7 damage. This move has moderate startup, with a very long lingering active hitbox, but a noticeable whiff endlag.

[kbd]Brute Force[/kbd] is the basic "punch", high damage and knockback, though slow windup, that can still blockbreak with wind. [kbd]Pebble Throw[/kbd] is jack of all trades, movement, combo ender or extender, and mix-up. Stomp then punch out a little pebble you can swap with. [kbd]Elbow Drop[/kbd] is an unblockable launch into the air and slam on the ground. Combo extender that can be used to cheese M1 trades, in the same realm as Rapid Punches.

Blazing Star can be used for movement via using it in neutral, mixup by swapping with the pebble mid move, or use the Black Flash which is STRICTLY a combo ender. Boogie Woogie is a clap that swaps the position of you and another. Perfect Swapping is performed by M1ing after a swap, which can restore the cooldown mostly and return the ult cost. Fakeout Swapping is performed by M1ing before a swap, which cancels the swap so no cooldown or ult is consumed. Feint Swapping is performed by swapping mid move which cuts the cooldown of the move in half before the hitboxes come out.

While it looks to be powerful in neutral, in execution, Boogie Woogie is usually unthreatening, as his followup is usually limited to M1s. Keeping this in mind, tracking and reacting to his movements while holding [BLOCK] is fine. Boogie Woogie essentially forces both targets to functionally stand still which means there's usually nothing of value, overall making Boogie Woogie a very fake neutral option. There are three ranges in which Boogie Woogie can be used: long-range, mid-range, and close-range.
This is the distance wherein Boogie Woogie is blockable. The Switcher can't extract much value out of doing this.

This is the range wherein Boogie Woogie is unblockable, but is too far to have any proper follow up. The Switcher may decide to front dash here, but with proper tracking, as well as the chase's really large whiff endlag, makes this option too unsafe.

This is the distance wherein Boogie Woogie is unblockable, and is within the range of a side-dash M1. This is usually the most disorienting and dangerous spot where Boogie Woogie can be used, but if the opponent preserves their sidedash, the startup of Boogie Woogie gives them enough time to interrupt his swap into a combo.

[b]Neutral options[/b] [b]-[/b] [i][b]Divine Dog[/b][/i] is your best neutral option in your kit, being uncancellable once used, blocking the opponent's view (which helps with going in for side dash M1s), and forcing them to sit and block for a moment. [i][b]Rabbit Escape[/b][/i] can be used as an M1 reset for much more damage if you catch the opponent with M1s when they fall after [i][b]Rabbit Escape[/b][/i] suspends them in the air (can put them in the air with uppercut + [i][b]Divine Dog[/b][/i] or [i][b]Well's Unknown Abyss[/b][/i]). [b]-[/b] [i][b]Nue[/b][/i] works best when used inside a combo due to its true ragdoll. This can be used as an M1 trading tool if you gain a short distance and then go back in and use [i][b]Nue[/b][/i]. You have to aim at the target's head for [i][b]Nue[/b][/i] to lock onto them. [b]Ten Shadows summons a bird-like Shikigami that dissapears after a short period of time.[/b] The range of this move can be extended if it is targeted on a player. The main use of Nue is being a combo tool, although also useable for neutral (to a degree). If hit, it will apply [b]True Ragdoll[/b] on the opponent for a decent amount of time. If summoned on a ragdolled player, Nue will travel faster. However, it cannot be summoned while [u][b]Rabbit Escape[/b][/u] is active.

Due to the [b]True Ragdoll[/b] that Nue applies on hit, it allows for [b]unevasiveable[/b] combos such as: Nue > Toad > Frontdash > 3 M1's > Rabbit Entrance Nue > Toad > Frontdash > m1 set Nue > Rabbit Entrance This move can also be used for [b]Evasive Bait[/b]. Downslam the opponent, and wait a short moment before summoning Nue, so the opponent cannot delay evasive to tank Nue. Although inconsistent, Ten Shadows can M1 the opponent on wake-up to keep them in place and allow Nue to hit them, regardless if they evasive or not. Nue can also be used alongside M1s. Because Blocking slows down movement significantly, they cannot walk out of Nue to dodge it, giving Ten Shadows the upper hand. Do keep in mind though that this only works if the opponent has wasted their side dash.
